items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: Sid Catlett and Dave were considered the tops of their times.

ctx.x: So I can say this -- very good. Before I met Bix, before I ever knew Bix existed, Dave Tough told me about King Oliver and Louis. He was way ahead of his time and he was just super drummer. In the beginning he was influenced by Baby Dodds. Let's see, there was Johnny Dodds was the clarinet player and his brother was Baby. They were in the King Oliver band, and Dave was very much influenced, by him. Of course, MS. DANCE: George Wettling was too. MR. FREEMAN: Yes, Of course they were. I say this with all due…
I had ever heard, and of course, Sid Catlett and Dave were considered the tops of their times.

Bear in mind that Dave Tough influenced people like the so-called modern drummers. Now, we in jazz, we musicians in jazz do not use categories. We do not put people into categories and I will go into that in a few minutes. We don't call a man a modern drummer or an avant garde drummer or a dixieland drummer. A man can either play or he cannot. This is what it's about and only musicians know this. Not critics, I am sorry to say, with the exception perhaps of a few, such as you and Stanley Dance, Leonard Feather.…
